criteria.text: The participant has a histologically confirmed malignancy that is metastatic or unresectable and for which standard curative or palliative measures do not exist or are no longer effective
The participant has a HER2-positive or HER2-expressing tumor determined by a CLIA-certified laboratory

The participant has HER2 1-3+ expression by IHC, or HER2 amplification by NGS or ISH, or if local testing is not feasible, submits archival tissue for central HER2 testing (unknown or negative HER2 testing makes them ineligible)

The participant has HER2 1-2+ expression by IHC, or HER2 amplification by NGS or ISH, or if local testing is not feasible, submits archival tissue for central HER2 testing (unknown or negative HER2 testing makes them ineligible)
The participant has histologically confirmed platinum resistant, high grade serous ovarian carcinoma (defined as radiographic progression < 6 months following the last dose of platinum therapy)
Platinum resistance is defined as radiographic progression < 6 months following the last dose of platinum therapy
The participant has HER2 IHC 1+ per local or central testing
The participant has at least one lesion suitable for biopsy without significant risk
The participant's disease is evaluable or measurable by RECIST version 1.1, and the biopsiable lesion is not the only RECIST-measurable lesion
The participant has had at least one prior line of cytotoxic chemotherapy
The participant can have received an unlimited number of additional lines of chemotherapy, targeted therapy, biologic therapy, or hormonal therapy
The participant has archival FFPE tissue available for central confirmation of HER2 testing
The participant is >= 18 years old
The participant has an ECOG performance status <= 1 (Karnofsky >= 70%)
The participant has a hemoglobin level >= 10.0 g/dL (within 21 days of randomization/enrollment)
The participant has not received transfusions with red blood cells or platelets within 1 week prior to screening assessment
The participant has an absolute neutrophil count >= 1,000/mcL (within 21 days of randomization/enrollment)
The participant has not received G-CSF within 1 week prior to screening assessment
The participant has a platelet count >= 100,000/mcL (within 21 days of randomization/enrollment)

The participant has a total bilirubin level <= 1.5 x institutional ULN (or <= 3 x ULN if they have documented Gilbert's syndrome or liver metastases at baseline) (within 21 days of randomization/enrollment)
The participant has an AST/ALT level <= 3 x institutional ULN (within 21 days of randomization/enrollment)

The participant has a creatinine level <= 1.5 x institutional ULN OR a GFR >= 51 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (using the Cockcroft-Gault Equation), unless data supports safe use at lower values (no lower than 30 mL/min/1.73 m^2) (within 21 days of randomization/enrollment)
The participant has an LVEF >= 50% by ECHO or MUGA scan within 28 days before randomization/enrollment

If the participant is HIV positive, they must be stable on their anti-retroviral regimen, healthy from an HIV perspective, have an undetectable viral load and a CD4 count >= 250 cells/uL within 7 days of enrollment, and not be receiving prophylactic therapy for an opportunistic infection or have had one in the past 6 months
If the participant has chronic HBV infection, their HBV viral load must be undetectable on suppressive therapy, if indicated
If the participant has a history of HCV infection, they must have been treated and cured, or if currently on treatment, they must have an undetectable HCV viral load
If the participant has brain metastases, they must be stable, off steroids, and at least 4 weeks from radiation at the time of registration

If the participant has a prior or concurrent malignancy, its natural history or treatment must not have the potential to interfere with the safety or efficacy assessment of the investigational regimen

If the participant has a known history or current symptoms of cardiac disease, or a history of treatment with cardiotoxic agents, they must have a clinical risk assessment of cardiac function using the NYHA Functional Classification and be better than class 2B

Women of child-bearing potential and men must agree to use highly effective contraception prior to study entry, for the duration of study participation, and for at least 7 months (WOCBP) or 4 months (men) after the last dose of study drug

Women of non-child-bearing potential (pre-menopausal with documented tubal ligation or hysterectomy, or postmenopausal defined as 12 months of spontaneous amenorrhea) are eligible. Females on HRT with doubtful menopausal status must use contraception if continuing HRT, or discontinue HRT to confirm post-menopausal status prior to enrollment
Male subjects must not freeze or donate sperm starting at screening and throughout the study period, and at least 4 months after the final study drug administration

Female subjects must not donate, or retrieve for their own use, ova from the time of screening and throughout the study treatment period, and for at least 7 months after the final study drug administration

The participant has the ability to understand and the willingness to sign a written informed consent document. Participants with impaired decision-making capacity who have a legally-authorized representative and/or family member available are also eligible

The participant has not had chemotherapy (including antibody drug therapy) within 4 weeks, except 1 week for weekly paclitaxel; 2 weeks or five half-lives for small-molecule targeted agents; or 6 weeks for nitrosoureas or mitomycin C
The participant has not had radiation therapy within 4 weeks
The participant has not had a major surgery within 4 weeks
The participant is not receiving any other investigational agents

The participant does not have a history of (non-infectious) ILD/pneumonitis that required steroids, does not have current ILD/pneumonitis, and suspected ILD/pneumonitis can be ruled out by imaging at screening

The participant does not have clinically severe pulmonary compromise resulting from intercurrent pulmonary illnesses, any underlying pulmonary disorder, autoimmune/connective tissue/inflammatory disorders with potential pulmonary involvement, or a prior pneumonectomy

The participant does not have a history of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to DS-8201a, the inactive ingredients in the drug product, olaparib, or severe hypersensitivity to other monoclonal antibodies
The participant is not receiving any medications or substances that are moderate or strong inhibitors or inducers of CYP3A

The participant does not have a medical history of myocardial infarction within 6 months before randomization/enrollment, does not have symptomatic CHF (NYHA class IIb to IV), and does not have troponin levels consistent with myocardial infarction as defined according to the manufacturer 28 days prior to randomization
The participant does not have a corrected QT interval (QTc) prolongation to > 470 ms (females) or > 450 ms (males) based on the average of the screening triplicate 12-lead ECG

The participant does not have multiple primary malignancies within 3 years, except adequately resected non-melanoma skin cancer, curatively treated in-situ disease, and other solid tumors curatively treated
The participant does not have an uncontrolled infection requiring IV antibiotics, antivirals, or antifungals
The participant has not received chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine within 14 days prior to eligibility

The participant does not have unresolved toxicities from previous anticancer therapy (other than alopecia) not yet resolved to grade <= 1 or baseline. Subjects with chronic grade 2 toxicities may be eligible per the discretion of the investigator after consultation with the sponsor medical monitor or designee
The participant does not have a psychiatric illness or social situation that would limit compliance with study requirements
The participant is not pregnant and is not breastfeeding
The participant has not received a live, attenuated vaccine within 30 days prior to the first dose of DS-8201a

P1.text: Patients must have histologically confirmed malignancy that is metastatic or unresectable and for which standard curative or palliative measures do not exist or are no longer effective

P2.text: Patients must have HER2-positive or HER2-expressing tumors determined by a Clinical Laboratory Improvement Act (CLIA)-certified laboratory.

P3.text:
HER2 1-3+ expression by IHC OR
    * HER2 amplification by next generation sequencing panel (NGS) or in situ hybridization (ISH) OR
    * If local testing is not feasible, patients will submit archival tissue for central HER2 testing to determine eligibility. Patients with unknown or negative HER2 testing will not be eligible

P4.text:
HER2 1-2+ expression by IHC OR
    * HER2 amplification by next generation sequencing panel (NGS) or in situ hybridization (ISH) OR
    * If local testing is not feasible, patients will submit archival tissue for central HER2 testing to determine eligibility. Patients with unknown or negative HER2 testing will not be eligible

P5.text: Patients must have histologically confirmed platinum resistant, high grade serous ovarian carcinoma. Platinum resistant is defined as radiographic progression \< 6 months following the last dose of platinum therapy

P6.text: Platinum resistant is defined as radiographic progression \< 6 months following the last dose of platinum therapy

P7.text: HER2 IHC 1+ per local or central testing

P8.text: There must be least one lesion suitable for biopsy without significant risk to the patient

P9.text: Patient disease must be evaluable or measurable by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1. Biopsiable lesion cannot be the only RECIST-measurable lesion

P10.text: Patients must have had at least one prior line of cytotoxic chemotherapy

P11.text: Patients can have received an unlimited number of additional lines of chemotherapy, targeted therapy, biologic therapy, or hormonal therapy

P12.text: Patients must have archival formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue available for central confirmation of HER2 testing

P13.text: Age \>= 18 years. Because no dosing or adverse event data are currently available on the use of DS-8201a in combination with olaparib in patients \< 18 years of age, children are excluded from this study

P14.text: Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status =\< 1 (Karnofsky \>= 70%)

P16.text: No transfusions with red blood cells or platelets are allowed within 1 week prior to screening assessment

P17.text: Absolute neutrophil count \>= 1,000/mcL (within 21 days of randomization/enrollment)

P18.text: No administration of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) is allowed within 1 week prior to screening assessment

P20.text: Total bilirubin =\< 1.5 x institutional upper limit of normal (ULN), (\< 3 x ULN in the presence of documented Gilbert's syndrome or liver metastases at baseline) (within 21 days of randomization/enrollment)

P21.text: Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) (serum glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase \[SGOT\])/alanine aminotransferase (ALT) (serum glutamate pyruvate transaminase \[SGPT\]) =\< 3 x institutional ULN (within 21 days of randomization/enrollment)

P22.text: Creatinine =\< 1.5 x institutional ULN OR glomerular filtration rate (GFR) \>= 51 mL/min/1.73 m\^2 unless data exists supporting safe use at lower kidney function values, no lower than 30 mL/min/1.73 m\^2 (using the Cockcroft-Gault Equation) (within 21 days of randomization/enrollment)

P23.text: Patients must have left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) \>= 50% by either an echocardiogram (ECHO) or multigated acquisition (MUGA) scan within 28 days before randomization/enrollment

P24.text:
Patients who are human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) positive may participate IF they meet the following eligibility requirements:

  * They must be stable on their anti-retroviral regimen, and they must be healthy from an HIV perspective
  * They must have an undetectable viral load and a CD4 count \>= 250 cells/uL within 7 days of enrollment
  * They must not be currently receiving prophylactic therapy for an opportunistic infection and must not have had an opportunistic infection within the past 6 months
  * HIV-infected patients should be monitored every 12 weeks for viral load and CD4 counts

P25.text: For patients with evidence of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, the HBV viral load must be undetectable on suppressive therapy, if indicated

P26.text: Patients with a history of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection must have been treated and cured. For patients with HCV infection who are currently on treatment, they are eligible if they have an undetectable HCV viral load

P27.text: Patients with brain metastases should be stable and off steroids and at least 4 weeks from radiation at the time of registration

P28.text: Patients with a prior or concurrent malignancy whose natural history or treatment does not have the potential to interfere with the safety or efficacy assessment of the investigational regimen are eligible for this trial

P29.text: Patients with known history or current symptoms of cardiac disease, or history of treatment with cardiotoxic agents, should have a clinical risk assessment of cardiac function using the New York Heart Association Functional Classification. To be eligible for this trial, patients should be better than class 2B

P30.text: The effects of DS-8201a and olaparib on the developing human fetus are unknown. For this reason and because HER2 antibody conjugated to a topoisomerase 1 inhibitor agents as well as PARP inhibitors are known to be teratogenic; thus, women of child-bearing potential and men must agree to use highly effective contraception (hormonal or barrier method of birth control; abstinence) prior to study entry, for the duration of study participation, and for at least 7 months (women of childbearing potential \[WOCBP\] only) after the last dose of study drug. Should a woman become pregnant or suspect she is pregnant while she or her partner is participating in this study, she should inform her treating physician immediately. Men treated or enrolled on this protocol must also agree to use adequate contraception prior to the study, for the duration of study participation, and 4 months after completion of DS-8201a and olaparib administration

P31.text: Women of non-child-bearing potential defined as pre-menopausal females with a documented tubal ligation or hysterectomy; or postmenopausal defined as 12 months of spontaneous amenorrhea (in questionable cases, a blood sample with simultaneous follicle-stimulating hormone \[FSH\] \> 40 mIU/mL and estradiol \< 40 pg/mL \[\< 147 pmol/L\] is confirmatory) are eligible. Females on hormone replacement therapy (HRT) and whose menopausal status is in doubt will be required to use one of the contraception methods outlined for women of child-bearing potential if they wish to continue their HRT during the study. Otherwise, they must discontinue HRT to allow confirmation of post-menopausal status prior to study enrollment. For most forms of HRT, at least 2-4 weeks will elapse between the cessation of therapy and the blood draw; this interval depends on the type and dosage of HRT. Following confirmation of their post-menopausal status, they can resume use of HRT during the study without use of a contraceptive method

P32.text: Male subjects must not freeze or donate sperm starting at screening and throughout the study period, and at least 4 months after the final study drug administration. Preservation of sperm should be considered prior to enrollment in this study

P33.text: Female subjects must not donate, or retrieve for their own use, ova from the time of screening and throughout the study treatment period, and for at least 7 months after the final study drug administration

P34.text: Ability to understand and the willingness to sign a written informed consent document. Participants with impaired decision-making capacity (IDMC) who have a legally-authorized representative (LAR) and/or family member available will also be eligible

P35.text: Patients who have had chemotherapy (including antibody drug therapy) within 4 weeks with the following exceptions: 1 week for weekly paclitaxel; 2 weeks or five half-lives, whichever is longer, for small-molecule targeted agents such as 5-fluorouracil-based agents, folinate agents, hormonal agents; or 6 weeks for nitrosoureas or mitomycin C

P36.text: Patients who have had radiation therapy within 4 weeks

P37.text: Patients who have had a major surgery within 4 weeks

P38.text: Patients who are receiving any other investigational agents

P39.text: Patients with a history of (non-infectious) interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis that required steroids, has current ILD/pneumonitis, or where suspected ILD/pneumonitis cannot be ruled out by imaging at screening

P40.text: Patients with clinically severe pulmonary compromise resulting from intercurrent pulmonary illnesses including, but not limited to, any underlying pulmonary disorder (i.e. pulmonary emboli within three months of the study enrollment, severe asthma, severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease \[COPD\], restrictive lung disease, pleural effusion, etc.), and any autoimmune, connective tissue or inflammatory disorders with potential pulmonary involvement (i.e. rheumatoid arthritis, Sjogren's, sarcoidosis, etc.), or prior pneumonectomy

P41.text: History of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to DS-8201a, the inactive ingredients in the drug product, olaparib, or severe hypersensitivity to other monoclonal antibodies

P42.text: Patients receiving any medications or substances that are moderate or strong inhibitors or inducers of CYP3A are ineligible. Because the lists of these agents are constantly changing, it is important to regularly consult a frequently-updated medical reference. As part of the enrollment/informed consent procedures, the patient will be counseled on the risk of interactions with other agents, and what to do if new medications need to be prescribed or if the patient is considering a new over-the-counter medicine or herbal product

P43.text: Patients with a medical history of myocardial infarction within 6 months before randomization/enrollment, symptomatic congestive heart failure (CHF) (New York Heart Association class IIb to IV), troponin levels consistent with myocardial infarction as defined according to the manufacturer 28 days prior to randomization

P44.text: Patients with a corrected QT interval (QTc) prolongation to \> 470 ms (females) or \> 450 ms (males) based on average of the screening triplicate 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG)

P45.text: Patients with multiple primary malignancies within 3 years, except adequately resected non-melanoma skin cancer, curatively treated in-situ disease, and other solid tumors curatively treated

P46.text: Patients with an uncontrolled infection requiring IV antibiotics, antivirals, or antifungals

P47.text: Patients receiving chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine will require a washout period of \>= 14 days to be eligible for the study

P48.text: Patients with unresolved toxicities from previous anticancer therapy, defined as toxicities (other than alopecia) not yet resolved to grade =\< 1 or baseline. Subjects with chronic grade 2 toxicities may be eligible per the discretion of the investigator after consultation with the sponsor medical monitor or designee (e.g., grade 2 chemotherapy-induced neuropathy)

P49.text: Patients with psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements

P50.text: Pregnant women are excluded from this study because DS-8201a is a HER2 antibody conjugated to a topoisomerase 1 inhibitor agent with the potential for teratogenic or abortifacient effects. Because there is an unknown but potential risk for adverse events in nursing infants secondary to treatment of the mother with DS-8201a, breastfeeding should be discontinued if the mother is treated with DS-8201a. These potential risks may also apply to other agents used in this study

P51.text: Patients who have received a live, attenuated vaccine within 30 days prior to the first dose of DS-8201a

rule.registry:
Patients who are human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) positive may participate IF they meet the following eligibility requirements:

  * They must be stable on their anti-retroviral regimen, and they must be healthy from an HIV perspective
  * They must have an undetectable viral load and a CD4 count \>= 250 cells/uL within 7 days of enrollment
  * They must not be currently receiving prophylactic therapy for an opportunistic infection and must not have had an opportunistic infection within the past 6 months
  * HIV-infected patients should be monitored every 12 weeks for viral load and CD4 counts

rule.registry: Women of non-child-bearing potential defined as pre-menopausal females with a documented tubal ligation or hysterectomy; or postmenopausal defined as 12 months of spontaneous amenorrhea (in questionable cases, a blood sample with simultaneous follicle-stimulating hormone \[FSH\] \> 40 mIU/mL and estradiol \< 40 pg/mL \[\< 147 pmol/L\] is confirmatory) are eligible. Females on hormone replacement therapy (HRT) and whose menopausal status is in doubt will be required to use one of the contraception methods outlined for women of child-bearing potential if they wish to continue their HRT during the study. Otherwise, they must discontinue HRT to allow confirmation of post-menopausal status prior to study enrollment. For most forms of HRT, at least 2-4 weeks will elapse between the cessation of therapy and the blood draw; this interval depends on the type and dosage of HRT. Following confirmation of their post-menopausal status, they can resume use of HRT during the study without use of a contraceptive method
